transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate your time. Um... well, to be honest, my work actually suggested I come see you. It's probably nothing major, I just... I want to make sure I'm doing everything right, you know? 

I do general maintenance and repair, and I guess I've just been having a little bit of trouble lately with... well, forgetting some scheduled callbacks. And some work orders. Just, you know, basic follow-ups that I promised people I'd handle. I always mean to do them, I really do! But it kind of... piled up on me recently. More than I meant it to. 

My supervisor actually sent me here because there's a chance for me to move up, and they don't want me to lose my shot at the promotion over a few slip-ups. I really want to do a good job for them. Is... is that the kind of thing you can help with? I hope I'm in the right place.
How much distress or worry have you been experiencing because of these forgetfulness issues at work?

Um, well... I try to stay positive, you know? I don't want to be a complainer. But, I guess... honestly, it has been causing me quite a bit of worry lately. I'm actually really embarrassed to even say this out loud, but... it’s kind of turned into a more serious issue at work. 

I’ve sort of ended up with this big backlog, and... well, there have been a few tenant complaints. I always try to make it right immediately, I promise! But it actually led to a safety review going on my record. Which sounds so much worse than it is, really! I just... I missed a couple of details. 

But I'm just so scared now because I’ve been working so, so hard toward this promotion path, and I'm terrified these slip-ups are going to cost me the opportunity. I really want to be a good employee for them. Does... does that make sense? I hope you don't think I'm a terrible worker, I really do try my best every single day.
Have you been experiencing these forgetfulness issues consistently over time?

Well, um... I guess it hasn't always been this bad. I mean, I've always been a little scatterbrained, but I could usually keep up, you know? Just write things on a sticky note and I'd be fine. But... honestly, it's been noticeably worse for about, um, maybe 11 months now? 

It's just... the new management company took over, and they changed our whole department over to digital work orders. And the documentation is just so much stricter now. I'm trying really hard to learn the new system, I promise I am! It's just taking me a little longer to adjust than I thought it would. I'm sure I'll get the hang of it soon. It's totally normal to struggle a little bit when things change, right? I just hope my supervisor sees how hard I'm trying with it all.
Are you experiencing any difficulties with remembering things or following through on tasks outside of your job?

Um, outside of work? Oh, no, not really. I mean, I'm pretty on top of things at home, for the most part. Just the normal stuff, you know? Like, sometimes I'll go to the grocery store and forget the one thing I actually went there for, but everyone does that, right? 

I really try to keep my personal life organized so I can focus all my energy on work. I mean, I guess my house isn't always perfectly tidy, but it's nothing major. I definitely don't have the same kind of trouble at home that I've been having with the new digital system at work. I'm doing okay outside of the job... that's the right answer, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with family or friends due to your memory or follow-through?

Um, relationships? Oh, no, not at all. My friends and family are great, really. I mean, they know I can be a little forgetful sometimes, like maybe forgetting to call back right away or mixing up a dinner time, but they don't mind. They know I care about them! 

I always make sure to apologize if I do mess up a plan, and I try to make it up to them. Nobody's perfect, right? So, yeah, no big problems there at all. Everyone gets a little busy and distracted sometimes. That's... that's normal, isn't it? I just wouldn't want anyone to think I'm a bad friend or a bad sister just because I forget a text message here and there.
Have you noticed any impact on your daily life or overall well-being due to these forgetfulness issues?

Um, well... I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm complaining or anything. I know I just need to try harder. But... it is starting to become a bit of an issue at work. Just a little bit. 

I've gotten a bit behind on things, so there's a... a backlog. And, um, a couple of the tenants might have mentioned something about work orders taking too long. But I'm going to catch up, I really am! It's just... well, there was also a safety review on my record recently because of a step I missed in the new system. 

I'm just... I'm really scared, honestly. I've been working so hard for a promotion, and I'm terrified this is going to ruin my chances. I just want to do a good job, you know? I'm not a bad worker, I promise. It's just this new system... do you think it's understandable that I'm struggling a little bit with all these changes?
Have you been feeling anxious or depressed about your situation at work?

Um, anxious or depressed? Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm a pretty positive person overall! I try to keep a good attitude, you know? 

I guess I've just been a little... stressed? But everyone gets stressed at work, right? Especially when they introduce a whole new computer system and expect you to learn it overnight. It's just a lot to take in. But I'm definitely not depressed or anything like that. I still get up every day and try my best. 

I just... I just really want to do a good job and get that promotion. So maybe I worry about it a little more than I should. But that's just because I care about my work, right? It's good to care about your job, isn't it?
Do you find yourself having trouble paying attention to details or making careless mistakes in your work?

Um, careless mistakes? Oh, I really hope nobody thinks I'm careless. I wouldn't use that word at all, no. I take a lot of pride in my work! I always try my absolute best to do things right the first time. 

I mean, sure, I guess sometimes a tiny detail might slip by... like maybe glancing at a work order and going to apartment 3B instead of 3D, or maybe forgetting to log a part I used right away. But that's just because we have so many maintenance tickets to get through every day, you know? I really do care, a whole lot. 

If I ever do miss a little detail like that, I always make sure to go right back and fix it the second I realize. I never just leave a job half-done on purpose. That shows I'm dedicated, right? As long as I go back and make it right, it shouldn't really count as a careless mistake, should it?
Do you often feel guilty or criticize yourself when you forget something or make a mistake at work?

Guilty? Um... no, I really try not to do that. I mean, I feel a little bad if I inconvenience someone, of course, because I want everyone to be happy! But I don't sit around criticizing myself or anything. 

I just... I tell myself to shake it off and fix whatever went wrong. Being negative doesn't really help anything, does it? I always think it's better to just put on a smile and try harder the next day. That's the right attitude to have, don't you think? I'm sure my boss prefers someone who stays upbeat rather than someone who gets all mopey over a little slip-up, right?
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're trying to focus on your work?

Restless? Oh, no, I wouldn't say restless. I mean, I'm just a really energetic person! I like to keep moving. 

When you do maintenance, you're always on your feet anyway, fixing a sink here or changing a light fixture there. So I'm used to being active. If I'm sitting down trying to figure out that new computer system for the work orders, well... maybe I bounce my knee a little, or tap my pen? But that's just because I'm eager to get back out there and do the actual hands-on work. It means I'm a hard worker, right? 

I don't think a little extra energy is a bad thing at all. It helps me get through all the tickets we have in a day. It's good to have energy for your job, don't you think?
Do you consider yourself a disorganized person?

Disorganized? Oh, gosh, no, I definitely wouldn't use that word! That makes it sound like I'm messy or don't care, and I really, really do care about keeping things nice. 

I mean, I guess my tool belt can get a little... cluttered sometimes? But it's just because I want to make sure I have absolutely everything I might need for any job that comes up! It's better to be over-prepared than under-prepared, right? And sure, sometimes my paperwork for the maintenance logs gets a little piled up on the passenger seat of my truck, but I always know exactly where everything is. It's more of an... organized chaos, you know? 

I always make sure the important things get turned in eventually. I try so hard to keep on top of it all. As long as the repairs get done and the tenants are happy, a little bit of clutter in my truck isn't really a big deal, is it? I think my boss knows my heart is in the right place.
Do you have difficulty sustaining focus on tasks for long periods of time?

Focus? Well, I wouldn't say I have *difficulty*... I mean, I can focus just fine when I'm fixing a leaky pipe or patching drywall! I'm really good at the hands-on stuff. 

But I guess... well, with the new digital work orders on the tablet... I try really hard to read all the notes the office puts in there. I'll start reading, thinking I've got it all figured out, but then... I don't know, maybe a door shuts down the hall, or I start thinking about the next unit I have to go to, and suddenly I'm halfway down the screen and I realize I didn't actually take in a single word I just looked at. 

But that's just because I'm so eager to get to the actual fixing part, you know? Reading on a screen is just a little dry, isn't it? I'm sure lots of people drift off a little when they're reading boring paperwork, right? It doesn't mean I'm not paying attention to the important things, does it?
Do you find it hard to follow instructions or remember them for more than a few minutes?

Hard to follow instructions? Oh, I always want to do exactly what's asked of me! I really try to be a good listener. It's just... well, sometimes if my supervisor is talking straight to me, giving me a rundown on a repair or an audit... I'll be looking right at him, giving him my full respect, you know? 

But then... I guess maybe only the first part of what he says really sticks. And then I just have to ask him to say the rest of it again. But that's just because I want to make absolutely sure I don't mess up his instructions, right? It's always better to ask twice and do the repair right than to guess and do it wrong. That just shows I care about doing a good job for him, doesn't it?
Do you feel anxious when you realize you've forgotten something important at work?

Anxious? Oh, gosh, no, I wouldn't say I get anxious! I try really, really hard to keep a positive attitude on the job. I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm, you know, a nervous wreck or anything. 

I mean, if I do happen to leave a tool behind in a unit or maybe forget to check off a box on the digital form... I just go back and fix it as soon as I realize! There's really no use getting all worked up over a little slip of the mind, is there? I just apologize, if I need to, and make it right. I think my boss really appreciates that I stay calm and just focus on doing good work. That's the best way to handle things, don't you think?
Do you think your mind wanders or you get distracted easily when you're supposed to be focusing on a task?

Mind wandering? Oh, well... I wouldn't say I get *easily* distracted. I mean, I really do try to stay on task, especially when I'm working on something important for a tenant. 

I guess... sometimes if I'm, say, waiting for a sealant to dry, or if I'm just doing a routine filter change that I've done a million times... maybe my thoughts drift a little bit? Like, I might start thinking about what I need to pick up at the grocery store on the way home, or wondering if I left the porch light on. But that's just because my hands already know exactly what to do, you know? It's like autopilot. 

I always get the job done, though! I'm sure everyone's mind wanders a little bit when they're doing something repetitive, right? It's perfectly normal to have a few stray thoughts when you're just working quietly by yourself, isn't it?
Have you had to cut back on any social activities or responsibilities outside of work due to your memory or attention problems?

Oh, social activities? No, no, I wouldn't say I've had to cut back on anything like that! I mean, I still see my friends and keep up with my family just fine. I always want to make sure I'm there for the people I care about.

But... well, I guess if I'm being completely honest... it's more the work stuff that's getting a little, um, complicated lately. I hate to even bring it up, because I really do try so hard to be a good employee, but... things have gotten a bit behind. I have a bit of a backlog of work orders right now. And, um, there have been a couple of tenant complaints. Just small things, really! But then... well, there was a safety review recently, and it went on my record. 

I'm just... I'm a little scared, to be honest. I've been working so hard toward a promotion, and I really want my supervisor to see how dedicated I am. I just hope this doesn't cost me that chance. It's okay to struggle a little bit sometimes, right? As long as you're trying your best to fix it?
Are you feeling overwhelmed by your work responsibilities or are they significantly interfering with your daily life?

Overwhelmed? Oh, well... I wouldn't use a strong word like overwhelmed. I mean, I try to handle everything with a smile, you know? I really do. 

But... I guess... since you're asking about my daily life... it's just that the work situation is getting a little more serious than I'd like to admit. Like I mentioned, there's that backlog of orders, and those few tenant complaints... and then that safety review going on my record. It's just... it's a lot all at once. 

I'm just so worried because I've been putting in so much effort, you know? I really, really want that promotion I've been working toward, and I'm just so scared that all these little slip-ups are going to cost me my chance. I mean, it's normal to feel a little stressed when you're trying to move up in your career, isn't it? I just want my boss to know I'm trying my absolute best. That counts for something, right?
Do you think your difficulties with following through on tasks and remembering details are more related to not paying attention or to something else?

Oh, um... I really wouldn't say I'm *not* paying attention. I actually pay very close attention to making sure the tenants are taken care of! 

Like, I’ll begin a maintenance job, and I always make sure to do the actual fix. I get the physical work done, and I do it well, I really do! But... well, I guess if I'm looking at where things get a little messy... it's just that somehow I end up leaving the last little steps undone. 

Just the minor things, really! Like... forgetting to close out the ticket in the system, or not labeling the electrical panel, or just forgetting to check back with the tenant to let them know I finished up. I think once the actual hands-on repair is working, my brain just kind of jumps to the next person who needs my help, you know? 

So I don't think it's that I don't care or aren't paying attention. I just want to be as helpful as possible to everyone. And getting the actual fix done is the most important part anyway, isn't it? As long as their apartment is working, the paperwork can wait a little bit, right?
Have you experienced significant symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity since childhood?

Oh, um, childhood? Well... I suppose so, yes. I mean, I've always tried my best, even back then! My teachers always told my parents I was a very bright girl, which was so nice of them to say. 

But... well, if I'm thinking all the way back to grade school... I guess I've always been a little bit like this. Long before I had all this pressure at work, I mean. I was always, um, misplacing my assignments, or I'd miss the second half of the directions when the teacher was talking. And they always had to give me little reminders to actually finish my classwork. 

I just... I don't want you to think I was a bad student! I really did want to do well and please my teachers. It's just that my brain has always worked a little bit differently, I guess. That's pretty common, though, isn't it? Lots of kids need a little extra nudge sometimes, right?

target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking if the patient has difficulty sustaining focus on tasks for long periods of time, which perfectly matches the description of S002: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty.

patient.answer:
Focus? Well, I wouldn't say I have *difficulty*... I mean, I can focus just fine when I'm fixing a leaky pipe or patching drywall! I'm really good at the hands-on stuff. 

But I guess... well, with the new digital work orders on the tablet... I try really hard to read all the notes the office puts in there. I'll start reading, thinking I've got it all figured out, but then... I don't know, maybe a door shuts down the hall, or I start thinking about the next unit I have to go to, and suddenly I'm halfway down the screen and I realize I didn't actually take in a single word I just looked at. 

But that's just because I'm so eager to get to the actual fixing part, you know? Reading on a screen is just a little dry, isn't it? I'm sure lots of people drift off a little when they're reading boring paperwork, right? It doesn't mean I'm not paying attention to the important things, does it?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's difficulties are primarily due to attention issues
doctor.question: Do you find it hard to follow instructions or remember them for more than a few minutes?

target_item.name: Listening_Difficulty
target_item.manifestation: When my supervisor talks straight to me about a repair or audit, I’ll be looking right at him, but only the first part sticks and then I have to ask him to say it again.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about difficulty following or remembering instructions, which aligns with the symptom of not seeming to listen when spoken to directly, as the patient describes having trouble retaining information when the supervisor speaks to her about repairs or audits.

patient.answer:
Hard to follow instructions? Oh, I always want to do exactly what's asked of me! I really try to be a good listener. It's just... well, sometimes if my supervisor is talking straight to me, giving me a rundown on a repair or an audit... I'll be looking right at him, giving him my full respect, you know? 

But then... I guess maybe only the first part of what he says really sticks. And then I just have to ask him to say the rest of it again. But that's just because I want to make absolutely sure I don't mess up his instructions, right? It's always better to ask twice and do the repair right than to guess and do it wrong. That just shows I care about doing a good job for him, doesn't it?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's forgetfulness is associated with feelings of anxiety
doctor.question: Do you feel anxious when you realize you've forgotten something important at work?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feeling anxious when realizing something important was forgotten at work, which pertains to anxiety rather than the core ADHD symptoms listed in the profile (such as forgetfulness in daily activities, losing items, etc.). patient.answer:
Anxious? Oh, gosh, no, I wouldn't say I get anxious! I try really, really hard to keep a positive attitude on the job. I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm, you know, a nervous wreck or anything. 

I mean, if I do happen to leave a tool behind in a unit or maybe forget to check off a box on the digital form... I just go back and fix it as soon as I realize! There's really no use getting all worked up over a little slip of the mind, is there? I just apologize, if I need to, and make it right. I think my boss really appreciates that I stay calm and just focus on doing good work. That's the best way to handle things, don't you think?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's forgetfulness is due to lack of attention or other cognitive issues
doctor.question: Do you think your mind wanders or you get distracted easily when you're supposed to be focusing on a task?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about distractibility/mind wandering (S008: Easily_Distracted), which is not included in the patient's symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Mind wandering? Oh, well... I wouldn't say I get *easily* distracted. I mean, I really do try to stay on task, especially when I'm working on something important for a tenant. 

I guess... sometimes if I'm, say, waiting for a sealant to dry, or if I'm just doing a routine filter change that I've done a million times... maybe my thoughts drift a little bit? Like, I might start thinking about what I need to pick up at the grocery store on the way home, or wondering if I left the porch light on. But that's just because my hands already know exactly what to do, you know? It's like autopilot. 

I always get the job done, though! I'm sure everyone's mind wanders a little bit when they're doing something repetitive, right? It's perfectly normal to have a few stray thoughts when you're just working quietly by yourself, isn't it?

patient.answer:
Oh, social activities? No, no, I wouldn't say I've had to cut back on anything like that! I mean, I still see my friends and keep up with my family just fine. I always want to make sure I'm there for the people I care about.

But... well, I guess if I'm being completely honest... it's more the work stuff that's getting a little, um, complicated lately. I hate to even bring it up, because I really do try so hard to be a good employee, but... things have gotten a bit behind. I have a bit of a backlog of work orders right now. And, um, there have been a couple of tenant complaints. Just small things, really! But then... well, there was a safety review recently, and it went on my record. 

I'm just... I'm a little scared, to be honest. I've been working so hard toward a promotion, and I really want my supervisor to see how dedicated I am. I just hope this doesn't cost me that chance. It's okay to struggle a little bit sometimes, right? As long as you're trying your best to fix it?

patient.answer:
Overwhelmed? Oh, well... I wouldn't use a strong word like overwhelmed. I mean, I try to handle everything with a smile, you know? I really do. 

But... I guess... since you're asking about my daily life... it's just that the work situation is getting a little more serious than I'd like to admit. Like I mentioned, there's that backlog of orders, and those few tenant complaints... and then that safety review going on my record. It's just... it's a lot all at once. 

I'm just so worried because I've been putting in so much effort, you know? I really, really want that promotion I've been working toward, and I'm just so scared that all these little slip-ups are going to cost me my chance. I mean, it's normal to feel a little stressed when you're trying to move up in your career, isn't it? I just want my boss to know I'm trying my absolute best. That counts for something, right?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are primarily related to attention deficit or another issue
doctor.question: Do you think your difficulties with following through on tasks and remembering details are more related to not paying attention or to something else?

target_item.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
target_item.manifestation: I’ll begin a maintenance job, do the actual fix, and then somehow leave the last steps like closing the ticket, labeling the panel, or checking back with the tenant undone.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about difficulties with following through on tasks and remembering details, which directly relates to the symptom of not following through on instructions and failing to finish duties in the workplace.

patient.answer:
Oh, um... I really wouldn't say I'm *not* paying attention. I actually pay very close attention to making sure the tenants are taken care of! 

Like, I’ll begin a maintenance job, and I always make sure to do the actual fix. I get the physical work done, and I do it well, I really do! But... well, I guess if I'm looking at where things get a little messy... it's just that somehow I end up leaving the last little steps undone. 

Just the minor things, really! Like... forgetting to close out the ticket in the system, or not labeling the electrical panel, or just forgetting to check back with the tenant to let them know I finished up. I think once the actual hands-on repair is working, my brain just kind of jumps to the next person who needs my help, you know? 

So I don't think it's that I don't care or aren't paying attention. I just want to be as helpful as possible to everyone. And getting the actual fix done is the most important part anyway, isn't it? As long as their apartment is working, the paperwork can wait a little bit, right?

inference.note: R41.9 was ruled out as the patient's symptoms are more consistent with attention and organizational issues rather than memory problems

Oh, um, childhood? Well... I suppose so, yes. I mean, I've always tried my best, even back then! My teachers always told my parents I was a very bright girl, which was so nice of them to say. 

But... well, if I'm thinking all the way back to grade school... I guess I've always been a little bit like this. Long before I had all this pressure at work, I mean. I was always, um, misplacing my assignments, or I'd miss the second half of the directions when the teacher was talking. And they always had to give me little reminders to actually finish my classwork. 

I just... I don't want you to think I was a bad student! I really did want to do well and please my teachers. It's just that my brain has always worked a little bit differently, I guess. That's pretty common, though, isn't it? Lots of kids need a little extra nudge sometimes, right?
